title: The Rarest Readiness
logline: A rescue crew drills the same response hundreds of times so that on the rare day someone is actually in trouble nobody has to think before moving, and in between handles the ordinary unpleasantness the job brings.
human_question: What does it take to be instantly ready for a danger that may never come?

situation.what_happens: A water rescue crew spends almost all of its time not rescuing anyone: drilling, checking equipment, watching, and dealing with the ordinary, unglamorous and sometimes repulsive parts of being the people called when something goes wrong. The drills exist so that the rare real moment requires no decision. Most days the readiness has nothing to do, and holding it anyway is the actual discipline.
situation.who_is_involved: The crew, professional or volunteer, and whoever trains them; the people they watch over, who mostly never know they were watched; the families of crew members; the services they hand casualties on to.
situation.what_is_at_stake: Someone's life, occasionally. Much more often: attention that cannot be allowed to lapse, on low pay or no pay, with nothing happening. For the film: the risk of filming a real emergency at the expense of the person in it.
situation.how_it_unfolds: A season runs on repetition, with competence maintained against boredom. Pressure comes from crowds, weather and the knowledge that the one incident will not announce itself. It ends either with a season in which nothing happened, which is the best outcome and the hardest to film, or with a real incident that the film must handle carefully. Reality decides which, and the film does not wish for the second.

concept_merge.why_together: C089 (the direct knowledges) contributes the ranking: of everything the sources describe, they say the hardest and rarest use is being able to act instantly and calmly when someone else is suddenly in danger, harder than the spectacular feats they also relate [C089-P4:L104–L108]. C101 (the direct-knowledge process) contributes how such capacities are said to be built, by slow, graduated, repetitive training, near before far and coarse before fine. C090 (the ten kinds of supernormal power) contributes the full list and the fact that the one mark reserved for the fully freed is not a feat at all but an even response to the repulsive and the alluring alike [C090-P4:L85–L87; C090-M:L13], which the crew's ordinary handling of the job's unpleasant parts can point at.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: Together they invert what the word 'power' suggests. The tradition's own ordering puts drilled, unspectacular readiness and an even response to what disgusts above anything dramatic, and it is explicit that nothing comes from wishing. A film about people who train for a day that may not come makes that ordering visible in secular terms, while presenting the extraordinary abilities only as what the texts describe.

concept_links.why: The sources rank acting calmly and instantly when someone is suddenly in danger as the hardest use of any of these trained states, and say that mere wishing achieves nothing [C089-P4:L104–L108]. The digest also requires that the miracle narratives be neither asserted as fact nor debunked, so the film presents them only as what the texts teach.

The digest describes the training as slow and graduated, coarse before fine and near before far, rather than sudden talent. Drilled readiness is an honest echo of that discipline, and the film does not claim the crew has anything the texts describe.

The list of ten runs from the spectacular to the ordinary, and the one kind said to belong to the fully freed alone is dwelling without revulsion toward the repulsive, without attraction to the alluring, and evenly toward both [C090-P4:L85–L87; C090-M:L13]. The crew's steady handling of what others avoid points at that ranking; the digest forbids turning the protection stories into a promise that good people are kept safe.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: Being ready to act calmly the instant someone is in danger is built from long, repetitive, unglamorous practice. In the texts' own ranking, that quiet readiness is harder and rarer than any spectacular feat.
what_must_be_real: A real service's real training and real duty. Any actual incident is filmed only with care for the people in it, never with danger staged or prolonged, and no one is presented as having any ability the texts describe or any attainment.
position_hint: middle, late: it reframes what the group's remaining material means by 'power' before the two films about withdrawal and letting go.
risks: Filming a real emergency at the expense of the person in danger
Implying the crew has any ability beyond trained skill
Sensationalising the unpleasant parts of the work, or making a symbol of anyone who does them
Long stretches of nothing happening, which is the honest subject and the hardest to sustain
drop_if: Filming a real response would compromise anyone's safety or privacy
No service will allow filming of training and waiting on their own terms

connections.note: Brought the least spectacular of the ten kinds, the even response to the repulsive and the alluring, and the ordinary work others turn away from.
From readiness for sudden danger to the practical readiness of setting affairs in order before a long absence.

selection.reason: Used by EPD-0096, and now carries the quiet end of the list of ten as well as the ranking of readiness.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
